main_text.head: VERSVS XVIII.

p.i: Ego tamen in Iehouah exultabo : gefliam in Deo salute mea.

main_text.p: Fidei ἀντεναγωγὴ est, quæ etiam summi mœroris remedium indicat.
Qui Deum habent Saluatorem, illis bona spe discutienda est trifticia, & exultandum in Seruatore Deo.
Ego uerò,inquit Propheta,Deũ salute, id est,salutis certissimũ auctorem habeo.
Est igitur mihi in Iehouah exultandũ præ gaudio. Idem uerò etiam aliis pijs, quorũ eadẽ fors est, faciendũ esse statuo.
Atque hoc est spe gaudere, Rom.12.12. gloriari in opprefsionibus, quòd hæc pa-tien-

page.notes: Reference mark "y" with "5" printed at the foot (line 22 area) belongs to the catchword line and was read as a signature-like mark; the marginal reference "Rom.12.12." appears inline at the end of the paragraph and is printed in the text line. The Greek words "ἀντεναγωγὴ" are copied as printed; the second Greek word is uncertain and may be read as "ἀντεναγωγή" with a different accent. "Pfal.144.13." and "Pfalm.67.6." are printed as inline references. The Hebrew-style name "Iehouah" is printed as such. The word "Iehouah" and "exultabo" are read clearly. Printing irregularities such as "decem millia parientes" and the spelling "trifticia" are left as printed. The final word "tien-" is a line-end hyphenated fragment carried to the next page.
